_comment: Every screenshot the guides use, retaken by scripts/screenshots.mjs against the app on a fresh docs seed (volt-app/scripts/seed-docs.ts). A shot is a console path, what to wait for, and optionally an element to crop to, elements to hide and clicks to make first. Images land in static/img/screens/<name>.png; guides show them with ![...](/img/screens/<name>.png).

shots.name: account-settings
shots.alt: The Account settings page, with the logo and colours at the top

shots.name: account-settings-trick-play
shots.alt: The Trick-play for Apple and smart-TV players card: the account default for new output profiles, then a switch for each output profile

shots.name: audit-log
shots.alt: The Audit log page listing recent changes, newest first

shots.name: dashboard
shots.alt: The Dashboard: five counts across the top, then the attention list, streams on air, the last seven days and recent output

shots.name: live-streams
shots.alt: The Live Streams board: counts across the top, then one row per running stream with its five gates

shots.name: monitoring
shots.alt: The Monitoring page: severity counts, the alert list and fleet activity

shots.name: multiview
shots.alt: Multiview: the output and viewer location choices, grid size, and a tile per running stream

shots.name: channels
shots.alt: The Channels list: type and status filters, then one row per channel with its type, status and a Start or Stop button

shots.name: channel-new
shots.alt: The New channel form: name and logo, Transcode or Packaging with the group, then the source or the renditions you send

shots.name: channel-status
shots.alt: A channel page: the overall status beside the name, the five gates under it, then the source and output players
shots._why: The docs seed leaves News 24 recorded as running with no encoder behind it, so its page shows real gates: starting just after the API comes up, a failed Server gate with the Diagnose banner after about 90 seconds.

shots.name: radio
shots.alt: The Radio list: status filters, then one row per station with now playing, signal, outputs and status

shots.name: events
shots.alt: The Events list: status filters, list and calendar views, then one row per event with its window, status, recording and replay settings

shots.name: fast-new
shots.alt: The New FAST channel form: name, video or audio, group and time zone

shots.name: fast-run-order
shots.waitFor: h3:has-text('What this run order does to a week')
shots.alt: A FAST channel's Run order: the library of titles and series on the left, what the run order does to a week, then the series slot and the film slot

shots.name: fast-week
shots.alt: The Week tab: seven days side by side, every programme of the coming week at its start time on the half-hour grid

shots.name: epg
shots.alt: The EPG list: one row per channel, station and event guide, with how many programmes it has, how far ahead it is filled and what is next

shots.name: loops-and-fillers
shots.alt: The Loops & Fillers page: the upload area at the top, then the list of loops and slates with a preview, what uses each one, its size and status
shots._why: The docs seed adds a slate (used by News 24) and a loop, so the list is not the empty state.

shots.name: graphics
shots.alt: The Graphics page: counts of templates, setups and what is on air, the four tabs, and the template library with a preview of each

shots.name: captions
shots.alt: The Captions page: the engine for the account at the top, then a card for each output profile with its languages and who uses it

shots.name: formats-and-reframing
shots.alt: The Formats and reframing page: output formats and what to keep in frame on the left, publish targets and when it runs on the right

shots.name: media-library
shots.alt: The Media Library page: the upload band at the top, the search, sort and filter chips, then the list of assets with their review, QC and availability

shots.name: media-library-exact-frame
shots.alt: The Media Library preview paused on exact frame 5, with its frame number and timecode over the picture

shots.name: media-library-find-details
shots.alt: Find details on a film: the search, the items Wikidata found with the film first, and the fields to tick beside what the asset has
shots._comment: Needs Wikidata reachable from the API, or WIKIDATA_API_BASE at a stand-in that answers wbsearchentities and wbgetentities (Wikimedia rate-limits busy shared addresses).

shots.name: media-library-find-details-link
shots.alt: Find details with a pasted link: the film's page on its site shown first, then the Wikidata result, and the fields to tick beside what the asset has
shots._comment: Needs a page at http://films.example/films/nosferatu with schema.org Movie JSON-LD that the API can fetch (a hosts entry to a stand-in, with GRAPHICS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_FEEDS=1 on the API), and WIKIDATA_API_BASE as for media-library-find-details. Reset Nosferatu's metadata to its title and rating PG first.

shots.name: recordings
shots.alt: The Recordings page: filter chips for channels, radio, events and what is recording now, then one row per source with its recordings, available range, content held and status

shots.name: recordings-exact-frame
shots.alt: A recording paused on an exact frame: the frame number and timecode over the picture, TC beside Position, and the exact first and last frames of the In and Out marks under the controls

shots.name: image-library
shots.alt: The Image Library: the folder tree on the left, the search box and filters at the top, and a grid of images with their usage type, size and folder

shots.name: review
shots.alt: The Review page: the queue of clips with their source, length, QC result and review state, one clip opened to show what was measured and the decision buttons

shots.name: share-links
shots.alt: The Share window: how to send it, how long it lasts, who can open it and a label, with the links already made for this stream listed below
shots._why: The Share window over the channel page; the window has no dialog role to crop to, so the shot is the whole page.

shots.name: encoding-profiles
shots.alt: The Encoding profiles page: the list of renditions with the form to add one, the New ladder card, and a ladder with its rungs and the preview of what a source would get

shots.name: watchfolders-on-prem
shots._why: Before the watchfolders shot: that one opens a folder, and the page is not reloaded between shots, so the list with its New watchfolder button is only there first.
shots.alt: The New watchfolder form with On-prem, at a site chosen: the name, the site, and the folder's path on the site's server

shots.name: watchfolders
shots.alt: A watchfolder's page: its path and Scan now button, the numbered rules (one with an image type) with the one that would win highlighted, the Try a filename box, and the queue of files that need a person

shots.name: storage
shots.alt: The Storage page: what this service can do at the top, the retention ladder, event data retention, the dry run, and the list of media with its state, tier and size

shots.name: storage-mirror-archive
shots.alt: The Mirror and Archive section of the Storage page: a NAS folder and an S3-compatible store as storage targets with their speed caps and read-back cadence, and the copies (originals, and a programme's recording with its metadata file) with their state, the reason a copy waits and what to do about it

shots.name: publishing-archive-copies
shots.alt: The Archive copies field of the account default: a NAS copied to when files land and with every recording, an object store copied to when they are published, each with Nightly and a choice of Original, Sidecars, Clips and HLS/DASH package, only between 22:00 and 06:00 in Sydney time

shots.name: sites
shots.alt: The Sites page: a site with its health, its hosts with what each server has and when it last reported, one approved and one waiting for approval, and the Add a host section

shots.name: workflows
shots.alt: The Workflows page: the counts of runs, the Map, Runs and Add-ons and triggers and Report tabs, and the pipeline map with its three lanes, stages and hooks

shots.name: workflows-report
shots.alt: The Workflows Report tab: the 24 hours, 7 days and 30 days choice, totals for the last 7 days, and the pipeline map with each stage's runs, error rate, p50 and p95 time, retries and most common error code, with QC selected

shots.name: content-types
shots.alt: The Content Types page: the list of types on the left with filters for what each is offered for, and the field editor for the chosen type on the right

shots.name: publishing-rules
shots.alt: The Publishing Rules page: the publishing points, and the account default with a preset picker and its Lifecycle and Access sections, each field with its padlock

shots.name: publishing-policy-locks
shots.alt: The Protection section of the account default: DRM, playback token lifetime, WAF profile, allowed referrer domains and concurrent streams, with DRM's padlock closed

shots.name: publishing-policy-check
shots.alt: Before you save, under the account default with DRM ticked: the titles it governs, how many are published and how many the save changes, and the conflict that blocks the save, DRM with MP4 download allowed

shots.name: publishing-metadata-rules
shots.alt: Metadata rules on the Publishing Rules page: two rules in order, each with its conditions, what it sets, how many titles it governs and arrows to move it, and the box to test a title

shots.name: publishing-metadata-rule-open
shots.alt: A metadata rule opened: its name, its condition Tags has any of premier-league, and the start of its policy with Geo access set to Australia and New Zealand and locked

shots.name: ingest-rules
shots.alt: The Ingest Rules page: the platform baseline, the account default, content type and source or folder rungs with their rules, then linked cloud accounts and webhooks

shots.name: channel-groups
shots.alt: The Channel groups page: the plan strip with what is shared out, then the table of groups with their workflow, output profile, share of the plan and events

shots.name: analytics
shots.alt: The Audience view: watching now, views, unique viewers, watch hours and peak concurrent across the top, then views and unique viewers by day

shots.name: analytics-rights-demand
shots.alt: The Rights demand view: the period and kind, blocked viewers, blocked requests, plays and requests after the window, then a world map shaded by blocked viewers

shots.name: analytics-rights-demand-title
shots.alt: One title chosen: each country with its blocked viewers, blocked requests and plays, and whether the title is licensed there

shots.name: plan-and-limits
shots.alt: The Plan & limits page: the plan name, three meters for channels and stations, shared out to groups and running at once, then the table of groups

shots.name: fleet-and-usage
shots._why: Shown as a customer account sees it (customerView): the server's setting names and machine names are only for whoever runs the Volt deployment (build queue 1.14-G4a).
shots.alt: The Fleet & Usage page: servers now, billable today, this month and all time across the top, one server with its load, then billable time by day

shots.name: payments
shots.alt: The Payments page: four provider cards, the products made from your access rules with each provider's id, and the viewer look-up

shots.name: on-demand-ads
shots.alt: The On-demand ads page: the last seven days at the top, then the account default with a pre-roll and mid-rolls every 10 minutes, house spots and the ad server

shots.name: social-accounts
shots._why: Shown as a customer account sees it (customerView): the server's setting names and machine names are only for whoever runs the Volt deployment (build queue 1.14-G4a).
shots.alt: The Social accounts page: one card per platform, YouTube with a linked sandbox account, Facebook, Instagram, Threads, TikTok and Dailymotion, and X off at the bottom with Use your own X app

shots.name: notifications
shots._why: Shown as a customer account sees it (customerView): the server's setting names and machine names are only for whoever runs the Volt deployment (build queue 1.14-G4a).
shots.alt: The Notifications page: the three delivery channels with a test button each, the sent list with one alert, the templates and your devices

shots.name: users-and-roles
shots.alt: The Users & Roles page on Admin users: the two-step sign-in policy, then the account's people with their roles, tier, two-step sign-in and status

shots.name: permissions-map
shots.alt: The Permissions map: one column per kind of user, one row per area of Volt, with None, View, Operate or Manage in each cell

shots.name: api-keys-and-apps
shots.alt: The API Keys & Apps page: the registered apps with their platform, key prefix and requests, then the server-to-server secret keys

shots.name: collections
shots.alt: The Collections page: the tree of collections on the left, and a sub-collection open on the right with its name, description, colour and parent, then its media in order

shots.name: collections-rules
shots.alt: A rule-based collection: the Rules card with two conditions and the live count, the order, and its media marked Rule or Added

shots.name: collections-access
shots.alt: The Access card of a collection: all apps, everywhere, a premium rule for Australia and New Zealand with its pass and the iOS app's own price, and members everywhere else

shots.name: collections-view-as
shots.alt: View as on a collection: the web player in Australia for a viewer not signed in, two titles locked with the pass that unlocks them and one blocked by rights, then the matrix of apps by regions

shots.name: encoding-queue

shots.name: genres
shots.alt: The Genres page: the genre list with the box to add genres, each genre with Retire and Remove, and beside it where the list is used and how changes land

shots.name: rights
shots.alt: The Rights page: summary tiles, the default for new assets, and the list of profiles with their territories, app icons, uses, access, window, asset count, agreement and status

shots.name: rights-block-message

shots.name: rights-profile
shots.alt: A rights profile: owner, territories as chips, app types as cards with icons and named apps, uses, access types, the window and the agreement, with where it plays and how assets got it beside them

shots.name: single-sign-on
shots.alt: The Single sign-on page: an OpenID Connect provider with its on switch, Test, Edit and Remove, an email domain waiting for its DNS record, and the redirect URI to give the provider
